terms.grammar: relinquō, relinquere, relīquī, relictum, with in mediō
evidence: Cic. Cael. 48: tantum in mediō relinquam (Lewis & Short s.v. relinquō)
terms.comment: Latin leaves the matter “in the middle”, open to all, where English leaves it in the air.

terms.gloss: be undecided, hang in the balance (of a person or a matter)
evidence: Traupman 110: pendeō, to be up in the air
terms.comment: Literally “hang”; of a person in doubt, often animī pendēre (see be in suspense).

phrases.latin: quod ego ut incompertum in mediō relinquam
phrases.english: which, as unverified, I shall leave open

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 110.
